convertibility_reason: Uses only CTrade standard library for order execution. No custom indicators, no external logic libraries, simple timer-based alternation between Buy and Sell. Fixed lot sizing with no complex money management.

other_exits: SL/TP set at order placement; no explicit close logic in EA code

custom_logic_notes: EA alternates between Buy and Sell on each timer event. Trigger==0 triggers a Buy and sets Trigger=1; Trigger==1 triggers a Sell and sets Trigger=0. There is no position existence check beyond the Trigger flag — the Trigger merely prevents repeating the same side consecutively, but does not verify whether the previous trade is still open. If a trade fails, Trigger does not change, so the same side will be retried on the next timer event. SL for Buy is placed below bid; SL for Sell is placed above ask — both using Point() * StopLossLevel. TP for Buy is above ask; TP for Sell is below bid — both using Point() * TakeProfitLevel. Timer interval is TimerTime * 100 milliseconds (not seconds — potential bug or intentional sub-second timer). OnTick is empty; all logic is in OnTimer.
python_conversion_notes: Timer-driven alternating Buy/Sell EA. No indicators to convert. Key conversion points: (1) Timer event must be simulated — use a schedule or polling loop at TimerTime*100ms intervals. (2) Trigger flag alternation is simple state tracking. (3) SL/TP are set at order submission using current bid/ask ± pip offsets — must use live bid/ask at time of order, not bar close. (4) No position existence check — only the Trigger flag gates entry. (5) Point() and _Digits are symbol-dependent; ensure proper pip/digit normalization in Python. (6) CTrade.Buy/Sell map directly to broker API market orders with SL/TP. (7) Note: timer interval is TimerTime*100 ms, not TimerTime seconds — verify if this is intentional or a bug before replicating.
